doc.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: How the rabbit became Bugs, and the animation cels he never kept
summary: His father's design was chosen to update an old rabbit character, and Mel Blanc suggested naming it Bugs after Bugs Hardaway. Animation cels were common around the house and he kept none.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well what happened was they had a cast of cartoon characters, one of them was a rabbit, I believe it was called Oswald. And it was a conventional rabbit. I mean its ears hung down and it went on all fours. And they wanted to update this character somehow, so the cartoonists all submitted their suggestions and ideas. And it turned out that my father’s was the one that was selected. And so Mel Blanc, the famous voice person, they were going to call it the Happy Rabbit originally. And Mel said, and he has quoted this in his book also, that he said well why don’t you name him after the guy that drew him and call him Bugs, after Bugs Hardaway. So that’s the true story.
Yeah, that’s pretty neat. Now they have all these — you know what cells are?

The animation cells? Well those were so plentiful and common when I was a kid that I didn’t think a thing about it. And I don’t have any. And they were around all the time. And they are very valuable now, and very expensive. And I don’t have any of those.
Yeah it’s funny when you think about what your parents do, that sometimes it doesn’t have significance until—
